title.narrative: Fighting Impunity for International Crimes in the Kasais
Rättvisa för internationella brott i Kasaierna

description.narrative: TRIAL international har tillsammans med Physicians for Human Rights utvecklat en insats som syftar till att bekämpa straffriheten för grova brott mot mänskliga rättigheter begångna under de senaste åren i Kasai-provinserna, inklusive, men inte uteslutande, sådana begångna inom ramen för dem väpnade konflikten 2016-2017. Detta innefattar att stärka förmågan hos aktörer inom, och partners till, det lokala rättssystemet att utreda, åtala och ställa till svars ansvariga. Verksamheten kommer att omfatta utbildning av personal inom den civila och militära rättskedjan, inklusive åklagare, domare, försvarare, rättstekniker, utredande polis, samt NGOs aktiva inom områdena. Projektet kommer även att coacha enskilda ärenden genom rättssystemet, till stöd för brottsoffer och relevanta instanser, för att möjliggöra effektiva och rättssäkra rättsprocesser, domar och uppföljning inklusive kompensation till brottsoffer.

The Partner, TRIAL international, in cooperation with Physicians for Human Rights, has developed this project with the aim to combatting impunity for serious human rights violations committed in recent years in the Kasaï provinces in the DRC, including, but not limited to, those committed within the context of the armed conflict 2016- 2017. This includes strengthening the capacities of actors within, and partners to, the national judicial and law enforcement authorities to investigate cases, prosecute suspects and bring perpetrators to justice. The activities will include training of civilian and military judicial functions, including prosecutors, judges, defense lawyers, forensic technicians, investigative police, as well as NGOs active in these areas. The project will also coach individual cases through the justice system, supporting victims of crimes and relevant judicial bodies, to enable effective and legal processes in conformity with the rule of law, judgements and compensation to victims of human rights abuses.

The overarching objective of the intervention is to contribute to the fight against impunity and to promote the access to transitional justice in the Kasai region. This is to be done by promoting access to justice to victims of human rights violations and by reinforcing the capacity of the judicial system and other stake holders relevant to reinforcing rule of law and equitable justice principles in the DRC.

sector.narrative: Justice, law and order policy, planning and administration

description.narrative:
In relation to the objective of victims assistance and access to justice 5 individual cases of international crimes were submitted to Congolese courts and resulted in a criminal trial where victims could participate and obtain the conviction of the perpetrator, and 18 mass crimes cases were submitted to Congolese courts, among which 3 cases resulted in a trial favourable to victims, 6 cases for which an investigation has been completed and 9 cases for which an investigation were ongoing at the time of the final report (May 2023).
In relation to the local capacity building 37 lawyers were trained and mentored on the representation of victims of international crimes before Congolese courts 31 doctors were trained on the documentation of physical and psychological evidence of torture, including sexual violence 29 human rights defenders were trained on the documentation of international crimes according to best practices and international standards 10 Congolese NGOs were mentored on the identification and sensitization of victims of international crimes and documentation of the violations in view of a judicial procedure before Congolese courts 32 police officers were trained on investigation techniques and 37 magistrates were trained on the investigation and prosecution of international crimes according to best practices and international standards.
After the training sessions, two networks (one in Kasaï Central and one in Kasaï) of multisector professionals were formed to support improved responses to sexual violence in Kasai in order to facilitate cross-sector collaboration on local investigations and prosecutions. Members of the networks include doctors, psychologists, lawyers, magistrates, judicial police officers, and representatives from local NGOs. The Kasaï Central network has met several times for discussions on issues such as information sharing between sectors, the definition of rape, treatment and medical care to survivors of sexual violence, and mental health care. The Kasaï network was established shortly before the submission of the final report.
In addition to above, the project contributed in many ways to the Transitional Justice Process both in Kasai and at the national level. This was done both financially to support to round table and other activities in the process and, more importantly, by active participation in the processes through for example selection and training of members of the Kasaï commission on transitional justice.
